preview: Cleveland beat Pittsburgh 27-24 at home, moving to 2-1 and handing the Steelers their first loss of the same record. Deshaun Watson threw for 268 yards and a touchdown on 24-of-33 passing, while Quinshon Judkins ran for 53 yards and a score. Aaron Rodgers put up 299 yards and three touchdowns but was intercepted twice, and Jaylen Warren's 93 rushing yards weren't enough to keep Pittsburgh unbeaten.

The Giants beat the Cardinals 36-24 at home, moving to 3-1 while Arizona fell to 1-3. Jameis Winston threw for 250 yards and three touchdowns on 18-of-29 passing, and Cam Skattebo added 58 rushing yards on 18 carries. Arizona's Jacoby Brissett countered with 166 yards and two touchdowns but was intercepted three times, and Jeremiyah Love's 63 rushing yards on 14 carries weren't enough to close the gap.

Dallas beat Houston 34-30 on the road, dropping the Texans to 0-4 while the Cowboys evened out at 2-2. Javonte Williams decided it on the ground, running for 62 yards and three touchdowns on 19 carries, and Dak Prescott added 335 passing yards on 32-of-45. C.J. Stroud threw for 347 yards and two scores in the loss, but Houston's 0-4 start is the story.

Carolina beat Detroit 32-26 at home, improving to 1-2 as the Lions fell to 2-1. Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns on 29-of-41 passing, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 122 yards and two more scores on 20 carries. Detroit got 412 passing yards and a touchdown from Jared Goff and 46 rushing yards and a score from Jahmyr Gibbs, but it wasn't enough.

Green Bay beat Tampa Bay 17-14 at Raymond James Stadium, dropping the Buccaneers to 0-4 while the Packers moved to 2-2. Jordan Love threw for 197 yards and two touchdowns on 22-of-30 passing with one interception, outdueling Jalon Daniels, who managed 148 yards with a touchdown and two picks on 19-of-27. Bucky Irving's 61 rushing yards on 16 carries led a Tampa Bay offense that couldn't convert enough to avoid the loss.

Indianapolis beat Washington 30–13 at the Commanders' home venue, dropping WSH to 1–3 while the Colts evened out at 2–2. Jonathan Taylor carried it, rushing for 95 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries, and Daniel Jones managed the game with 143 passing yards. Washington's day was summed up by its leading rusher: Marcus Mariota, who threw for 186 yards with a touchdown and an interception, gained 35 yards on his lone carry.

Kansas City beat Las Vegas 30-27 on the road, moving to 4-0 while the Raiders fell to 3-1. Kenneth Walker III decided it, rushing for 177 yards and two touchdowns on 22 carries, and Patrick Mahomes added 225 passing yards and two scores. Kirk Cousins threw for 365 yards and two touchdowns with an interception in the loss, while Ashton Jeanty managed just 58 yards on 15 carries.

Seattle beat the Los Angeles Chargers 30-23 at home, moving to 3-1 and handing Los Angeles its fourth loss in four games. Sam Darnold threw for 168 yards and two touchdowns with an interception, and Emanuel Wilson ran for 81 yards and a score on 21 carries. Justin Herbert finished 19-of-31 for 189 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions for the 0-4 Chargers.

The Los Angeles Rams beat the Philadelphia Eagles 24-20 at Philadelphia, leaving both teams at 2-2. Kyren Williams decided it, rushing for 80 yards and two touchdowns on 16 carries while Matthew Stafford threw for 317 yards and two interceptions.

Minnesota beat Miami 15-10 at home to move to 4-0, dropping the Dolphins to 0-4. Kyler Murray led the Vikings with 247 passing yards on 27-of-37, while Aaron Jones Sr. added 94 rushing yards on 20 carries. Miami got 100 rushing yards and a touchdown from Ollie Gordon II, but Malik Willis managed just 85 passing yards on 9-of-17 in the loss.

Drake Maye threw for 269 yards and three touchdowns as New England beat Buffalo 29-26 on the road, handing the Bills their first loss and dropping both teams to 2-2 and 3-1 respectively. Maye outdueled Josh Allen, who finished 23-of-33 for 253 yards with a touchdown and an interception, while James Cook III ran for 75 yards and a score in the loss.

Baltimore beat Tennessee 24-18 at home, dropping the Titans to 0-4 while the Ravens moved to 3-1. Lamar Jackson threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns on 15-of-20 passing, and Derrick Henry added 73 rushing yards and a score on 23 carries. Cam Ward matched Jackson's 222 passing yards with a touchdown and an interception for Tennessee, which got 48 rushing yards and a touchdown from Tony Pollard.

Atlanta beat New Orleans 45-24 at the Saints' home venue, dropping New Orleans to 1-3 while the Falcons moved to 2-2. Bijan Robinson ran for 145 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries, and Michael Penix Jr. threw for 223 yards and a score on 15-of-20 passing. Tyler Shough finished 30-of-48 for 286 yards and a touchdown, and Alvin Kamara scored twice on the ground, but the Saints' 1-3 start is the story.

Tampa Bay beat Dallas 24-16 at Dallas, dropping the Cowboys to 2-3 and moving the Buccaneers to 1-4. Bucky Irving carried 21 times for 165 yards and a touchdown, outgaining a Dallas backfield that got 45 yards and a score from Javonte Williams. Dak Prescott threw for 316 yards but was intercepted twice on 42 attempts, and the loss left the host Cowboys a game under .500.

Baltimore beat Atlanta 30–23 on the road, riding Tyler Huntley's 201 passing yards and two touchdowns on 24-of-32, plus Derrick Henry's 102 rushing yards on 24 carries. Michael Penix Jr. threw for 240 yards and a score and Bijan Robinson ran for 86, but Atlanta's home offense couldn't match Baltimore's balance.

Green Bay beat Chicago 31–7 at home, moving both clubs to 3-2. Jordan Love led the Packers, completing 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards and two touchdowns, while MarShawn Lloyd ran for two more scores on 31 yards. Chicago managed just 108 passing yards from Case Keenum, who threw an interception, with D'Andre Swift providing the lone touchdown on the ground.

The New York Jets beat the Cleveland Browns 17-12 at home, moving to 2-3 and dropping Cleveland to 3-2. Geno Smith threw for 182 yards and a touchdown on 17-of-30 passing, while Braelon Allen carried 24 times for 116 yards and a score. Deshaun Watson managed just 155 yards on 15-of-33 passing with a touchdown for the Browns, who got 44 rushing yards from Quinshon Judkins.

Denver beat the Los Angeles Chargers 23-17 at LAC's home venue, dropping the Chargers to 0-5 while the Broncos improved to 3-2. Bo Nix threw for 123 yards and a touchdown, and J.K. Dobbins ran for 68 yards and a score on 18 carries to decide it. Justin Herbert managed just 121 yards with a touchdown and an interception on 14-of-24 passing, and Kimani Vidal's 57 rushing yards and a touchdown weren't enough to keep Los Angeles winless.

Detroit beat Arizona 45-21 on the road, dropping the Cardinals to 1-4 while the Lions improved to 3-2. Jared Goff threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns, and Jahmyr Gibbs carried 25 times for 151 yards and two more scores. Jacoby Brissett countered with 292 yards and three touchdowns on 29-of-47 passing, but Arizona's ground game never answered — Jeremiyah Love managed just 22 yards on 12 carries.

Houston beat Tennessee 26–3 at the Titans' home venue, dropping Tennessee to 0–5 and moving the Texans to 1–4. C.J. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a touchdown on 26-of-34 passing, and Woody Marks ran for 62 yards on 15 carries. Cam Ward managed 170 yards on 23-of-36 with an interception, and Tony Pollard's 52 rushing yards led a Titans offense that produced three points.

PIT 34, IND 22 — the Steelers won at home to move to 3-2, dropping the Colts to 2-3. Aaron Rodgers threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns on 22-of-31 passing, and Jaylen Warren ran for 101 yards and a score on 15 carries. Daniel Jones threw for 267 yards on 24-of-44 for Indianapolis, but Jonathan Taylor managed just 45 yards on 15 carries.

The New England Patriots beat the Las Vegas Raiders 45-17 at home, moving both teams to 3-2. Drake Maye threw for 374 yards and four touchdowns on 26-of-34 passing, and Rhamondre Stevenson added 64 rushing yards and a score. Kirk Cousins finished with 243 yards and a touchdown on 19-of-28 for Las Vegas, which got 27 rushing yards from Ashton Jeanty.

Minnesota beat New Orleans 23-13 at the Saints' home venue, moving the Vikings to 5-0 and dropping New Orleans to 1-4. Kyler Murray threw for 229 yards and a touchdown on 24-of-30 passing, while Aaron Jones Sr. ran for 113 yards and a score on 25 carries. Tyler Shough was intercepted twice and held to 96 yards on 16-of-25 passing, though Kendre Miller found the end zone on the ground.

Jacksonville beat Philadelphia 19-17 at home to move to 4-1, dropping the Eagles to 2-3. Trevor Lawrence led the Jaguars with 331 passing yards and two touchdowns on 24-of-39, while Bhayshul Tuten added 72 rushing yards on 22 carries. Jalen Hurts threw for 220 yards and a score on 21-of-40 for Philadelphia, which got just 14 rushing yards from Dameon Pierce.

San Francisco beat Seattle 32-29 at Seattle to move to 5-0, dropping the Seahawks to 3-2. Brock Purdy threw for 189 yards and two touchdowns, and Christian McCaffrey's 68 rushing yards on 11 carries helped the 49ers stay unbeaten. Sam Darnold threw for 195 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions, and Emanuel Wilson ran for 61 yards and a score in the loss.

Buffalo brings the league's No. 5 quality rank and a plus-20.0 run differential into Los Angeles, where the No. 18 Rams are .500 and riding a one-game win streak. Matthew Stafford has thrown for 317, 390 and 327 yards in his last three, while Josh Allen's Bills are coming off a 29-26 home loss to New England. James Cook III (421 rushing yards) and Puka Nacua (125 receiving yards last out) are the names to watch.

Denver beat Seattle 17-14 at home, moving to 4-2 and dropping the Seahawks to 3-3. The Broncos won it on the ground and on defense: J.K. Dobbins carried 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown, while Bo Nix managed just 107 passing yards on 17-of-27 — and still came out ahead because Sam Darnold threw two interceptions on a 27-of-51, 278-yard day. Jaxon Smith-Njigba was the game's best receiver with 134 yards in the loss.

Arizona beat the Rams 18-16 at LAR's home venue, dropping both clubs to 2-4. Jacoby Brissett threw for 218 yards on 24-of-35 passing with an interception, while Bam Knight ran for 80 yards on 15 carries to pace the Cardinals. Matthew Stafford countered with 222 yards and two touchdowns on 25-of-33 passing, and Kyren Williams added 50 rushing yards on 10 carries, but it wasn't enough to keep Los Angeles from the loss.

Cleveland beat Baltimore 13-10 at home, moving both clubs to 4-2. The Browns' defense held the Ravens to 10 points and limited Derrick Henry to 58 rushing yards on 17 carries, well below his 144-yard Week 1 outburst and the 68-plus he'd posted in every game since. Tyler Huntley threw for 165 yards and a touchdown in the loss, while Deshaun Watson managed 164 yards on 16-of-26 passing for Cleveland.

Bryce Young threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards and a score as Carolina beat Philadelphia 25-14 on the road. The Panthers improved to 3-2 while the Eagles fell to 2-4. Tanner McKee threw for 215 yards and a touchdown in the loss, with Dameon Pierce adding 35 rushing yards and a score.

Caleb Williams threw for 305 yards and a touchdown on 30-of-36 passing as Chicago beat Atlanta 31-23 on the road, dropping the Falcons to 2-4 while the Bears improved to 4-2. Michael Penix Jr. threw for 225 yards and three touchdowns in the loss, with Bijan Robinson adding 61 rushing yards on nine carries.

Green Bay beat Dallas 23-13 at home, moving to 4-2 while dropping the Cowboys to 2-4. Jordan Love threw for 276 yards with a touchdown and an interception on 23-of-41 passing, and the Packers defense picked off Dak Prescott twice — Prescott finished 34-of-54 for 258 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions. Dallas got its only touchdown on Javonte Williams' 41-yard day on 11 carries, while Pierre Strong Jr. led Green Bay on the ground with 28 yards on 11 carries.

C.J. Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns as the Houston Texans beat the Jacksonville Jaguars 34-31 on the road, dropping Jacksonville to 4-2 and lifting Houston to 2-4. Trevor Lawrence answered with 306 yards and four touchdowns on 24-of-41 passing, but his one interception helped decide a game that swung on a single possession. Chris Rodriguez Jr. led Jacksonville on the ground with 55 yards on 11 carries; Woody Marks paced Houston with 56 yards on 15 carries.

Kansas City beat the Los Angeles Chargers 22-6 at home to move to 5-0, dropping the Chargers to 0-6. Kenneth Walker III decided it, rushing for 128 yards and both Chiefs touchdowns on 19 carries, while Patrick Mahomes went 23-of-30 for 272 yards and an interception. Justin Herbert threw 37 times for 204 yards and a pick, and the Chargers' leading rusher was Herbert himself, with 26 yards.

The New Orleans Saints beat the New York Giants 34-27 at NYG's home venue, improving to 2-4 while dropping the Giants to 3-2-1. Tyler Shough threw for 144 yards and three touchdowns on 16-of-30 passing, and Kendre Miller ran for 70 yards on 20 carries to pace New Orleans. The Giants got 243 passing yards, a touchdown and an interception from J.J. McCarthy, who also led the team in rushing with 26 yards on two carries.

Pittsburgh beat Tampa Bay 26-19 on the road, dropping the Buccaneers to 1-5 while the Steelers improved to 4-2. Aaron Rodgers went 33-of-49 for 253 yards, two touchdowns and one interception, and Jaylen Warren's 50 rushing yards led a Pittsburgh ground game that kept the ball away from a Tampa Bay offense that got 164 yards and a touchdown but two interceptions from Jalon Daniels. Bucky Irving's 46 yards on 19 carries was the best the Buccaneers could manage on the ground.

Tennessee beat Indianapolis 26–20 on the road, dropping the Colts to 2-4 and improving the Titans to 1-5. Daniel Jones threw for 269 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions on 22-of-42 passing, while Jonathan Taylor ran for 94 yards and a score on 21 carries in the loss. Cam Ward finished 11-of-22 for 102 yards, a touchdown and an interception, and Tony Pollard added 76 rushing yards on 19 attempts for the Titans.

The San Francisco 49ers beat the Washington Commanders 23-17 at home, moving to 6-0 while Washington fell to 1-4-1. Brock Purdy threw for 264 yards and a touchdown on 21-of-29 passing, and Christian McCaffrey supplied both 49ers touchdowns on the ground with 64 rushing yards on 16 carries. Jayden Daniels kept Washington close with 300 passing yards and two touchdowns on 29-of-40, but the Commanders' 1-4-1 record leaves them well adrift of unbeaten San Francisco.

The Chicago Bears beat the New England Patriots 30-24 at home Thursday to move to 5-2, dropping New England to 4-3. Caleb Williams outdueled Drake Maye, throwing for 308 yards and two touchdowns on 22-of-33 passing, while Maye countered with 321 yards, two scores and an interception. D'Andre Swift carried 22 times for 78 yards and a touchdown as Chicago improved to 5-2.

Cincinnati beat Baltimore 35-13 on the road Sunday, improving to 4-2 while dropping the Ravens to 4-3. Joe Burrow decided it with 292 passing yards and four touchdowns on 22-of-30, outdueling Tyler Huntley, who threw for 298 yards with one touchdown and one interception on 23-of-34. Derrick Henry managed just 45 yards on 17 carries as Baltimore's ground game never got going.

Cleveland beat Tennessee 27-24 on the road, moving the Browns to 5-2 while the Titans fell to 1-6. Deshaun Watson threw for 308 yards, Quinshon Judkins ran for 96 and two scores, and Tony Pollard's 129 rushing yards and three touchdowns weren't enough for a Tennessee team that has now lost six of seven.

Detroit beat Green Bay 20-17 at home, moving to 4-2 and dropping the Packers to 4-3. Jared Goff threw for 303 yards and two touchdowns on 22-of-32 passing, while Jahmyr Gibbs carried 29 times for 116 yards to control the game. Jordan Love countered with 274 yards, two touchdowns and an interception on 27-of-45, but Green Bay's ground game never got going — Josh Jacobs managed just 36 yards on 11 carries.

Minnesota beat Indianapolis 16-10 at home to stay unbeaten at 6-0, dropping the Colts to 2-5. The Vikings' defense held Daniel Jones to 108 passing yards and picked him off once, while Jonathan Taylor's 95 rushing yards and a touchdown were most of what Indianapolis managed. Kyler Murray threw for 150 yards and a score, and Jordan Mason added 68 on the ground as Minnesota stayed atop the competition.

Seattle beat Kansas City 20–3 at home, handing the Chiefs their first loss of the season and dropping them to 5-1 while the Seahawks improved to 4-3. Sam Darnold outplayed Patrick Mahomes, throwing for 257 yards and a touchdown to Mahomes' 165 yards and an interception, and Emanuel Wilson's 100 rushing yards and a score carried a Seattle offense that kept Kansas City out of the end zone entirely.

The Los Angeles Rams beat the Las Vegas Raiders 35-21 at Las Vegas, dropping both teams to 3-4. Matthew Stafford threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns on 23-of-29 passing, and Kyren Williams ran for 99 yards and a score. Kirk Cousins threw for 295 yards and two touchdowns on 26-of-44 for the Raiders, who got 27 rushing yards from Mike Washington Jr.

Miami beat the Jets 28-25 at the Jets' home venue, moving the Dolphins to 1-5 and dropping New York to 2-5. Malik Willis threw for 208 yards and two touchdowns, and Ollie Gordon II carried 25 times for 103 yards and a score as Miami outlasted a Geno Smith day of 287 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. Braelon Allen ran for 104 yards in the loss.

The New York Giants beat the Houston Texans 27-21 at Houston's home venue, moving to 4-2-1 while the Texans fell to 2-5. Cam Skattebo ran for 124 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries, and J.J. McCarthy threw for 252 yards on 20-of-28 passing to hand Houston its fifth loss in seven games. C.J. Stroud finished 17-of-28 for 153 yards and two touchdowns, with Woody Marks adding 66 rushing yards on 19 carries.

Atlanta beat San Francisco 29-20 on Sunday, handing the 49ers their first loss and dropping them to 6-1 while the Falcons improved to 3-4. Michael Penix Jr. threw three touchdowns on 25-of-34 passing for 213 yards, and Atlanta's defense picked off Brock Purdy twice — Purdy still threw for 288 yards and a score on 27-of-40. The win snaps Atlanta's skid against the NFC's best and gives the 3-4 Falcons a signature result at home.

The Carolina Panthers beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home to reach 3-3, dropping Tampa Bay to 2-5. Bucky Irving carried 24 times for 106 yards and two touchdowns, but Baker Mayfield threw for just 64 yards on 11 attempts as the Buccaneers' passing game never got going. Bryce Young's 163 yards and a touchdown came with two interceptions, and Chuba Hubbard managed only 33 yards on seven carries — yet Carolina still came out ahead.

Dallas beat Philadelphia 38-31 at the Eagles' home venue, dropping Philadelphia to 2-5 while the Cowboys moved to 3-4. Dak Prescott threw three touchdowns on 15-of-27 passing for 212 yards, and Javonte Williams carried 25 times for 155 yards and a score. Philadelphia's Tanner McKee went 23-of-35 for 211 yards with a touchdown and an interception, while Saquon Barkley managed 62 yards and a touchdown on just seven carries.

Dallas (3-4, ranked #18) hosts Arizona (2-5, #28) on Sunday with both clubs below .500 and the Cardinals carrying a -9.43 run differential against Dallas's 1.29. Javonte Williams is the form play: 155 rushing yards in the Cowboys' 38-21 win at Philadelphia on Oct. 26, his best of the last five. Arizona's Trey McBride has 111 receiving yards in the Week 8 loss to Denver, but the Cardinals have dropped four of five and sit 28th of 32 in quality rank.

Atlanta (3-4) and Tampa Bay (2-5) both carry one-game win streaks into Sunday, but the Falcons sit 19th in quality rank against the Bucs' 22nd. Michael Penix Jr. has been steady through the air, throwing for 213, 225 and 240 yards over his last three games. Drake London is the hotter hand, coming off 66 and 62 yards after a 118-yard outing on Oct. 11.

Buffalo (5-1, ranked #4) can tighten its grip near the top of the league, while Baltimore (4-3, ranked #16) arrives on a two-game skid after a 35-13 loss to Cincinnati. James Cook III has been the engine for the Bills, averaging 125.4 rushing yards over his last five games. Zay Flowers is Baltimore's counterweight, coming off 137 yards against the Bengals and 118 two weeks earlier.

Both teams sit at 5-2, but Pittsburgh owns the better quality rank (#6 to Cleveland's #8) and a plus-2.14 run differential against the Browns' minus-1.86 — and the Steelers carry a three-game win streak into their home venue. Deshaun Watson is coming off 308 passing yards in Cleveland's 27-24 win at Tennessee, though his previous three outings sat at 164, 155 and 268. The Browns won the last meeting 27-24 in Cleveland on Oct. 1, so this one decides the season series.

Jacksonville (4-2, ranked #9 of 32) hosts a Colts team on a three-game skid at 2-5, with Indianapolis sitting at #25 in quality rank and a -3.71 run differential against Jacksonville's 8.33. Trevor Lawrence has thrown for 306 and 331 yards in his last two games, while Daniel Jones comes off a 108-yard outing for Indianapolis. Jonathan Taylor has been steady on the ground for the Colts, logging 95, 94 and 95 yards in three of his last four.

Denver's three-game win streak runs straight into the AFC's #3 team: the 5-1 Chiefs, whose lone loss is the only blemish on a 5-1 last-ten. Patrick Mahomes has cooled noticeably, throwing for 165 yards on Oct. 25 after 272 on Oct. 18 and 382 on Sept. 20. The host Broncos sit 5-2 and ranked #7 of 32, but their 0.43 run differential against Kansas City's 6.67 says the records are closer than the teams.

The Chargers arrive at 0-6 and ranked last in the league (#32), with a -10.17 run differential that dwarfs the Rams' +1.57 mark at #17. Los Angeles' offense has leaned on Justin Herbert, whose passing yardage has slid to 204, 121 and 189 over his last three games after a 226-yard outing on Sep 27. The host Rams counter with Kyren Williams, who ran for 99 yards on Oct 25 after 80 and 88 in the two games before that.

The Jets sit at 2-5 and have dropped two straight, while the Raiders are 3-4 but riding a four-game skid into a game at the Jets' home venue. Geno Smith has been efficient for New York with 1,623 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and just 2 interceptions, though Garrett Wilson's form has swung hard — 104 and 107 yards in two of his last five, but 26 and 44 in the two most recent. Kirk Cousins has thrown for 1,877 yards with 16 touchdowns and 5 interceptions for Las Vegas, and Brock Bowers has been steady with at least 70 receiving yards in four straight.

The NFL's last unbeaten team, 6-0 Minnesota, puts its perfect record and No. 1 quality ranking on the line at 4-2 Detroit, which has won two straight. Jared Goff has been dealing for the Lions, topping 300 passing yards in three of his last four games, including 412 on Oct. 4. Amon-Ra St. Brown's 153-yard outing against Green Bay on Oct. 25 is the hottest recent number on either side.

The 4-3 Patriots, ranked 15th of 32, visit a Miami team sitting 30th at 1-5 and riding a one-game win streak into Sunday. Drake Maye has thrown for 321, 235 and 374 yards in his last three outings, while Rhamondre Stevenson's 93 receiving yards on Oct. 22 gave New England another outlet. Miami's minus-9.83 run differential against New England's plus-2.43 frames the gap between these two clubs.

Philadelphia (2-5) arrives on a five-game losing streak and a -6.86 run differential, while Washington (1-4) sits just below at #29 of 32 with a -6.67 differential — a matchup between two of the league's weakest clubs, staged at Washington's home venue. Jayden Daniels has thrown for 300 and 199 yards in his last two dated outings, the brightest recent number either side brings. Saquon Barkley's 62 yards on Oct. 26 followed 8 on Oct. 4, and Tanner McKee has passed for 211 and 215 in his two most recent games.

Cincinnati hosts Tennessee with the Bengals riding a two-game win streak and ranked #10 of 32 in quality, while the Titans sit at #31 with a 1-6 record. Joe Burrow has thrown for 1,653 yards and 15 touchdowns against just 3 interceptions, and Tee Higgins is coming off 148 receiving yards in the Bengals' 35-13 win at Baltimore. Tony Pollard has been Tennessee's one reliable engine, rushing for 129 yards last week and 478 on the season.
